chunks: And Abū Ḥamzah al-Thumālī narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام that he said:

Whoever withholds the right of a Muslim while he is able to give it to him, out of fear that if that right leaves his hand he will become poor, then Allah, Mighty and Exalted, is more capable of impoverishing him than he is of enriching himself by withholding that right.

key_terms.حَقَّ: a due right or entitlement owed to another person
key_terms.مَخَافَةَ: fear or apprehension motivating the wrongful withholding
key_terms.مُسْلِمٍ: a Muslim whose right must be honored and not denied
key_terms.يَفْتَقِرَ: to become poor or fall into poverty
key_terms.يُغْنِيَ: to make oneself rich or self-sufficient
key_terms.يُفْقِرَهُ: to cause him to become poor

ai.seo_question: What does Islam say about withholding someone else’s financial right out of fear of becoming poor?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that withholding another Muslim’s due right out of fear of poverty is a grave moral failing. It affirms that provision and impoverishment are in Allah’s control, and that a person cannot secure wealth for himself through injustice.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3691 - Abu Hamzah Al-Thumali narrated from Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) that he said:

"Whoever withholds the right of a Muslim while he is able to give it to him, out of fear that if he lets go of that right he might become poor, then Allah (swt), the Mighty and Exalted, is more capable of making him poor than he is of enriching himself by withholding that right."
